claims.text: A high-throughput combinatorial synthesis approach can systematically vary elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing the elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce measurable changes in mechanical properties.
Changes in individual Hf or Nb concentration will correlate with local changes in hardness.
Changes in individual Hf or Nb concentration will correlate with local changes in elastic modulus.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a uniform equiatomic composition.
Previous fixed-composition studies typically synthesized uniform equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Gradient deposition or additive manufacturing can generate spatially varying HfNbTaTiZr compositions.
Nanoindentation arrays or micro-compression can rapidly evaluate local mechanical properties across the composition gradient.
Local changes in elemental percentages are expected to alter phase distribution.
Local changes in elemental percentages are expected to alter grain-boundary characteristics.
Local changes in elemental percentages are expected to alter defect concentrations.
Variation in individual elemental content modifies the alloy's microstructure and defect landscape.
Changes in microstructure and the defect landscape modify dislocation movement.
Modified dislocation movement and strengthening mechanisms affect hardness.
Modified microstructure and defect-mediated strengthening affect elastic modulus.
Increasing the concentration of a strengthening element may measurably increase hardness relative to the equiatomic baseline.
Subtle composition changes may produce effects too small to distinguish experimentally.
Overlapping effects from multiple elements may mask each element's individual contribution.
Adequate compositional resolution and mechanical-testing sensitivity are necessary to resolve composition-property relationships.
The magnitude of mechanical-property changes is uncertain because of interactions among elements and the scale of composition variation.
